digest.component_or_area: codebase-wide comment relocation and documentation refactoring
propositions: ~2,033 lines of recoverable comments across 439 files in src/rebar are categorized by taxonomy destination: history to tickets, architecture to ADRs, logic to code, contracts to schema, leaving only proximate just-in-time context inline.
Self-referential prose explaining the 800-line module cap occupies 28 sites in the reconciler and closes a loop at outbound_differ.py:164, creating a secondary burden that relocations must address.

Three files (_store/event_append.py, reducer/_processors.py, signing.py) carry load-bearing comments documenting replay-compatibility and security invariants that cannot be relocated and must be preserved on do_not_move lists.

Verified-stale comments at six sites contradict current code state (e.g., deterministic floor documented as P1-P9 while DET_CHECKS runs P1-P11; Anthropic constraints marked stale in structured.py) and must be corrected in place where they document live invariants.
All non-KEEP comment units must be dispositioned exactly once as RELOCATE/DELETE/KEEP/DO_NOT_MOVE/CORRECT-IN-PLACE, with do_not_move lists appended to .joe-janitor/tools.md before each shard lands.

Measured net recovery across six shards is ~85 comment/docstring lines (output of work, not target), with relocation-dominated changes where substantial prose moved verbatim to ADRs 0062-0069 and collapsed to citations rather than deleted.
